content.text: {"headline":"Approve R1 (peak overtime plus deflection on both queues, ₹4,284), but bring in the duty manager now: it is the best plan available yet still only reaches 60.9% against the 80% target for 13:00-15:00.","why":"The surge is driven by the P1 UPI switch outage (INC-20261006-6998). Payments calls are running +90% over forecast, with upi_payment_failed at 2.56x normal. Staffing and handle time are on plan, so this is a demand problem. Doing nothing leaves 13:00-15:00 at 30.8% service level, with payments at 19.1% and abandons at 21.7%. R1 combines four measures: overtime for 21 payments agents at the 13:30-14:30 peak, an IVR outage message, 20% chat deflection on both queues, and callbacks and break delays on both queues. Together these lift the window to 60.9%, with payments at 54.2% and general at 73.7%. Abandons drop to 9.3% and the rest of day reaches 83.9%. No policy is breached. Escalation is required because 60.9% is below the 70% escalation line (ESC-02). No option on the table reaches target, so further help such as outage resolution, wider comms or extra resource needs the duty manager.","trade_offs":["Versus P4 (₹3,372, 55.2%): R1 costs ₹912 more for about 6 points of service level. Most of that gain comes from extending deflection, callback and break delays to the general queue, which lifts general from 68.7% to 73.7%.","Versus R2 (₹4,644, 60.7%): R2 is ₹360 dearer for essentially the same result. Its abandon rate is slightly lower (9.0% vs 9.3%), but it needs 28 agents on a compressed 45-minute overtime slot, which is harder to fill.","Versus P1, the no-cost plan (30.3%): it does not help. Callbacks and break delays alone cannot absorb outage-driven demand, and payments slips to 17.2%.","Risk to general: R1 delays general breaks until 14:00 and deflects general calls. General still holds 73.7%, which is better than under no action (56.2%)."],"watch":"Check how many of the 21 payments agents accept the overtime offer. A shortfall will pull service level below 60.9%. Track the UPI incident status: if it resolves before 15:00, payments demand should fall and the overtime may be cut back. If it runs past 15:00, the window and plan need revisiting with the duty manager. Also watch payments service level (target 54.2%) and abandons (around 9.3%) through 13:30-14:30."}
